assertion.statement: Every nonsingular curve E_ell:y^2=x(x-ell)(x+3ell) with nonzero rational ell has no geometric CM, since its classical elliptic j is35152/9, a nonintegral rational number; the same holds for its quadratic twists.
assertion.objects: The classical elliptic j-invariant of E_ell and its quadratic twists, not the quaternionic moduli coordinate also denoted j.
assertion.hypotheses: ell is nonzero and rational; the displayed Weierstrass equation is used.
assertion.quantifiers: Every nonzero rational ell and every quadratic twist.
assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic zero over Q and its algebraic closure.
assertion.uniformity: The invariant j is independent of ell; this conclusion does not provide a uniform open-image index.
assertion.constants: c4=208ell^2, discriminant=2304ell^6, j=35152/9;9 does not divide35152.
assertion.normalizations: Use the classical elliptic Weierstrass c4^3/discriminant invariant and the full CM order, including nonmaximal orders.
assertion.exceptional_cases: ell=0 excluded because the curve is singular; no claim about the separate CM generator curve or the quaternionic coordinate.
assertion.limit_order: Compute nonsingular invariants first; use monic integral CM class polynomials to rule out geometric CM before invoking open image.

supplier.statement: For an imaginary quadratic order, the singular moduli are roots of a monic integral class polynomial, hence are algebraic integers.

available_assertion.statement: For an imaginary quadratic order, the singular moduli are roots of a monic integral class polynomial, hence are algebraic integers.
available_assertion.objects: Classical elliptic singular moduli of imaginary quadratic orders.
available_assertion.hypotheses: The elliptic curve has geometric complex multiplication by an imaginary quadratic order.
available_assertion.quantifiers: Every imaginary quadratic order, including nonmaximal orders.
available_assertion.parameter_range: Negative order discriminants; elliptic curves in characteristic zero.
available_assertion.uniformity: Algebraic integrality for all such singular moduli.
available_assertion.constants: No numerical height bound or discriminant estimate used.
available_assertion.normalizations: Use the classical elliptic Weierstrass c4^3/discriminant invariant and the full CM order, including nonmaximal orders.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: No maximal-order restriction; this is not a formula for a quaternionic Hauptmodul.
available_assertion.limit_order: Fix the CM order and form its class polynomial.
